source.title: When Will the Tokens End? Graph-Based Forecasting for LLMs Output Length
source.authors: G. Piotrowski; Mateusz Bystronski; Mikolaj Holysz; Jakub Binkowski; Grzegorz Chodak; T. Kajdanowicz

page_placements.theme: Response-level properties of the upcoming output encoded before or early in generation

record.file_problem: The paper text is present through its references, but the abstract opening is fragmented: it begins mid-sentence. No other cutoff is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures prediction of remaining response length from hidden states. It does not measure future-token content, whether that content shapes intervening tokens, or causal use of look-ahead. Its discussion cites Future Lens but does not test that finding.
record.gate_note: The paper reports length-prediction errors, which bear on hidden-state information about future output length, not on the claim versions’ future-token content or causal steering. It also reports that accuracy changes with distance from the end and that prediction is less accurate for particularly long or short outputs, but those figure-based results do not establish future-token representation or causal use. The selected layers (8–15) are stated as chosen based on prior work, not as a result of this study.
record.test_reason: The study trains regressors on mid-layer hidden states of three 7–8B instruct models to predict how many tokens remain (MAE/NMAE vs TRAIL). That is a scalar about output length, not the identity of tokens several positions ahead (V2). It involves no verse, no intervention, no test of pre-caching versus side effect, and no look-ahead tasks. Future Lens is cited only as motivation and as an analogy in the Discussion. The length-decodability result is a related construct and is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors say hidden states encode generation progress and remaining length, and that the layerwise graph regressor beats TRAIL on MAE and NMAE for all three models. They also say the method predicts length, not upcoming content, and that reliability drops at extreme lengths. They frame the result as analogous to Future Lens foresight, abstracted as a scalar.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains regressors on hidden states to estimate remaining output length; it does not reproduce future-token decoding or causally intervene on a candidate future token. It uses the TRAIL length-prediction setup as a baseline.
record.method_sensitivity: Prediction accuracy varies with token position; the paper says MAE decreases toward the sequence end and prediction is less accurate for particularly long or short outputs. These claims are described in the text, with the plotted position-wise values only in Figure 2.

fits_no_version.finding: Remaining output length is decodable from layers 8–15 hidden states of Gemma-7B-it, Mistral-7B-Instruct and Llama-3-8B-Instruct. The graph regressor lowers MAE relative to TRAIL in all three models (e.g., Gemma 15.25 to 9.49). Per the text (Figure 2), error falls toward the end of the sequence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Instruct-model hidden states carry decodable information about remaining response length (a progress signal), without implying token-level look-ahead or causal planning.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 4: Student Research Workshop)
record.problems: The paper says the dataset uses 1,000 prompts and notes this may limit generalizability. It predicts remaining length rather than upcoming content, reports no causal interventions, and does not report uncertainty estimates. Figure 2 is described qualitatively without numerical position-wise results in the text.

untested.parts: All parts: no frontier model, no verse, no rhyme representation or intervention.
Decoding of future token identities; only remaining length is predicted.
Whether features are computed for later positions rather than as a side effect.
Rhyme planning in open models; the open models here are not studied on verse.
Look-ahead in reasoning, chess or Sokoban.
Whether plans are shallow or incidental versus steering generation; no causal tests.

record.verdict_notes: This is a systems-motivated, scheduling-oriented workshop paper. It reports no uncertainty estimates and uses 1,000 Alpaca prompts. The NMAE values for the graph models are implausibly small relative to MAE, and the text and table disagree on Mistral NMAE. No row should link to any version.

versions.untested_parts: Rhyme-word representation before a line and causal intervention changing the line.
Decodability of future token identities several positions ahead; the study predicts remaining length, not token identities.
Whether features are computed because they help later positions rather than as a side effect of next-token prediction.
Rhyme planning and its interventions in open-weight models.
Look-ahead in multi-step reasoning, chess, Sokoban, or other tasks.
Whether apparent plans are shallow, incidental, or causal drivers of generation.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: The discussion connects length prediction to Future Lens, but the experiments neither test the defined versions nor use future-token decoding as a tool.

tranche.reason: Remaining-length prediction measures a related scalar construct, not future-token identity, causal planning, or another defined claim version.

source_check.notes: The listed rows faithfully reproduce Table 1 but measure predictor performance, not a defined planning effect. Table 1 gives Mistral Large/Small NMAE as 0.0114/0.0046; Results pairs Small NMAE with Large MAE. The unusually low reported NMAEs warrant caution.
